checks.name: first durable edit is sent at once; edits made while it is in flight form the next batch in order
batch identity, members and bytes are persisted before the first send and survive a renderer crash
a long offline dependency chain is split by operation and byte limits into ordered, strictly validated batches
one invalid operation in the middle rejects the whole batch with no partial commit, ACK or broadcast
a PostgreSQL error after batch rows were written rolls everything back; the original batch commits once later
server process killed inside the open transaction leaves no rows; retry after restart commits the same batch once
server killed after COMMIT before replying: the retry returns the original result and other devices catch up from PG
a connection dropped after COMMIT is resent by Chromium itself; the batch receipt answers with the original ACK
lost ACK followed by an aborted local confirmation keeps the batch; each retry returns the same version
renderer crash after the server committed but before the client confirmed: the reopened page resends the original batch
same batch ID with different members or bytes is refused; a committed operation cannot be repacked into a new batch
the same batch delivered concurrently on two connections commits once and both get one version
a batch formed before sharing stopped is refused as stale; after reopening its members become recovery drafts
a batch committed before sharing stopped, whose ACK was lost, is reconciled by receipt and not turned into a draft
commit racing stop-sharing in PostgreSQL: every batch is either in the frozen version or refused
two tabs share one sequence: one batch carries both tabs’ dependent edits in order and commits as one version
two tabs sending at once keep one batch in flight; nothing is sent twice or overtakes an unconfirmed batch
a stale tab writing after a reopen produces a draft and never enters a new batch
